newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY RADIO NOON HEADLINES - OCT 25.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY RADIO NOON HEADLINES - OCT 25.

text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:
- The government commissioner preparing the conditions of a planned energy price increase said the just solution would be a price rise not exceeding inflation rate.
- The World Association of Hungarians (WAH) denied what Secretary of State Csaba Tabajdi had said that WAH only represents conservative political forces and not Hungarians living abroad.
- The employers in the Interest Coordination Council refused the draft laws affecting the social security.
- Hungarian IFOR soldiers have already reconstructed 15 bridges destroyed by war in ex-Yugoslav states.

- Hungary and Switzerland have never got to an agreement about the property of Hungarian Jews killed by the Nazis, said Janos Fekete who in 1950 was chairman of a committe responsible for Hungarian property which remained abroad after World War Two.
- The police is questioning Marta Tocsik, a former advisor of the state privatisation agency who allegedly received irregular payment of 804 million forints from APV.
